evidence.quote: the Committee decided to continue purchasing additional agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $40 billion per month and longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $45 billion per month.

reaffirmed its expectation that a highly accommodative stance of monetary policy will remain appropriate for a considerable time after the asset purchase program ends and the economic recovery strengthens.
Apart from temporary variations in energy prices, inflation is running somewhat below the Committee’s longer-run objective of 2 percent.
However, at 7.7 percent, the unemployment rate remains elevated.
The Committee also remains concerned that restrictive fiscal policies may slow economic growth and job creation in coming months.
as we see a period in which the labor market is doing better, and we have reason to think it might be stronger, then we might reduce accommodation at that point.

parsed.rationale: The Chair reaffirms ongoing $85 billion monthly purchases and near-zero rates with threshold guidance, citing elevated unemployment, below-target inflation and fiscal drag; mild hawkish hints come from discussion of possibly adjusting the purchase pace and financial-stability costs.
